result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_gnr_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a growing network with redirection (GNR): a random tree grown by link copying. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_gnr_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a growing network with redirection (GNR): a random tree grown by link copying. title: >- [Graph.add_gnr_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Add a growing network with redirection (GNR): a random tree grown by link copying. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a growing network with redirection (GNR): a random tree grown by link copying. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L11819-L11919){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_gnr_graph( n, p, seed=None, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Growing network with redirection](../assets/graphs/add-gnr-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three growing networks with redirection on eight nodes, drawn as trees with the first node at the top and every arc pointing from a newer node to an older one. Each new node picks a random target and, with probability p, links to the node that target points at instead. At p=0 the tree is deep and stringy, at p=0.5 the first node collects 5 arcs, and at p=1 every arc is redirected to it, giving a star." width="100%"} Adds nodes one at a time. Each new node picks an existing node uniformly at random and, with probability `p`, links instead to the node that one links to (the first node links to nothing, so picking it never redirects). Following a link lands on a node in proportion to how many links it already has, so redirection works like preferential attachment without anyone knowing the degrees: the in-degrees follow a power law with exponent `1 + 1 / p`. With `p=0` the result is a random recursive tree. The model is due to Krapivsky and Redner; the process follows NetworkX's `gnr_graph()`. Each edge points from the new node to the older node it links to, so in a directed graph every node but the first has one out-edge and all paths lead to the first node. In an undirected graph the same edges are added without their direction. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. GNR graphs are useful for: - modeling the web or citation networks, where new pages link to what they find by following links - a local mechanism that produces power-law in-degrees - random directed trees whose hubs grow with `p=` ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. [p]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability of redirecting each new link to the chosen node's target, between `0` and `1`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is negative, or `p=` is not between `0` and `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two hundred nodes joined by `199` edges into one weakly connected piece make a tree, with all edges pointing toward the first node: ::: {#d14b6844 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_gnr_graph(n=200, p=0.5, seed=3) graph.count_edges(), graph.is_weakly_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (199, True) ``` ::: ::: More redirection makes bigger hubs, measured by the largest in-degree: ::: {#1af3c3c5 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} [ max( ec.Graph(directed=True).add_gnr_graph(n=200, p=p, seed=3).get_in_degree(v) for v in range(1, 201) ) for p in (0.0, 0.5, 0.9) ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [10, 30, 96] ``` ::: :::
